Operator:
Good day, and welcome to the Nexlify Third Quarter Fiscal 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are in listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question and answer session. To ask a question, you will need to press star then one on your touchtone phone. To withdraw your question, press star then two. Please be advised that today's call is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you, Operator. Good afternoon, everyone, and welcome to Nexlify's third quarter fiscal 2024 earnings call. Joining me today are Sarah Chen, CEO; Mike Patel, CFO; Lisa Wong, CTO; and David Kim, Chief Revenue Officer.

Before we begin, I'd like to remind you that this call contains forward-looking statements within the meaning of federal securities laws. These statements are subject to risks and uncertainties, and actual results may differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings, including our most recent Form 10-Q and 10-K, for a complete discussion of risks and uncertainties.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Sarah Chen.

Sarah Chen:
Thank you, Alex, and good afternoon, everyone. I'm thrilled to report on Nexlify's outstanding performance in the third quarter of fiscal 2024. We hit significant milestones, fueled by robust demand for our Nexlify Horizon platform and flawless execution across our strategic priorities.

Our focus this quarter centered on five key areas: advancing our product roadmap, issuing next-quarter ARR guidance, optimizing CAC trends, bolstering our cash runway, and driving free cash flow generation.

On the product front, we launched game-changing features like Nexlify AI Predict and Flows 2.0, with exciting initiatives like Horizon on deck. For guidance, we're projecting strong sequential ARR growth. CAC continues to trend down thanks to our PLG motion, our cash position gives us multi-year flexibility, and free cash flow remains a highlight of our efficiency.

Mike will unpack these in greater detail shortly. Overall, we're confident in sustaining this momentum to create enduring shareholder value.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Mike Patel to review the financials.

Mike Patel:
Thank you, Sarah. As Sarah highlighted, we delivered a powerhouse quarter. Revenue came in at $212 million, up 28% year-over-year. Gross margin expanded to 82%, reflecting the scalability of our platform, while non-GAAP operating income reached $52 million.

We're ramping investments in R&D to fuel innovation and broaden our offerings, all supported by a rock-solid cash position that enables opportunistic pursuits like tuck-in acquisitions.

Let me dive deeper into those five key areas Sarah outlined, starting with our product roadmap update.

I'm excited to share more on our product roadmap, which powered our impressive 28% year-over-year ARR growth this quarter, pushing total ARR past $850 million. Nexlify's RevOps platform leads in sales automation and customer engagement, serving over 12,000 customers worldwide—from mid-market firms to Fortune 500 giants in fintech and healthcare. Our net retention rate climbed to 118% this quarter, up 200 basis points year-over-year, thanks to product-led growth and expansions into AI modules.

Kicking off with recent launches: In Q2, we introduced Nexlify AI Predict, our generative AI toolkit for sales forecasting and lead scoring, built on fine-tuned Llama 3 models and our proprietary data lake. Early adopters—35% of our top 500 customers by ACV—saw 42% faster pipeline velocity and 27% shorter sales cycles, based on NPS surveys at 68. This generated $45 million in upsell ARR from seat expansions, with average cross-sells of 1.8 modules per customer. It's on par with Salesforce Einstein or HubSpot Breeze AI, but our real-time data integration across CRM, marketing, and service tools sets us apart.

Momentum carried into last month's Nexlify Flows 2.0, a low-code workflow builder with Zapier-style integrations and 150+ connectors to Snowflake, ServiceNow, and Okta. It exploded in adoption: 62% of Q3 new sign-ups chose it at onboarding, boosting activation rates 15% and slashing time-to-value to under seven days from 14. This has helped us grab eight points of mid-market SMB share per Gartner's 2024 Magic Quadrant for Sales Force Automation, outpacing Pipedrive and ActiveCampaign.

Looking ahead, our multi-product push emphasizes extensibility. Nexlify Horizon, our agentic AI platform, hits beta next quarter. These autonomous agents manage full revenue ops—from LinkedIn prospecting (GDPR/CCPA compliant) to contract negotiation via NLG on a decade of deal data. Pilots with an EMEA telco delivered 35% higher win rates on $500K+ deals. Priced at $50 per user per month as an add-on, we target 20-25% Year 1 attach rates, akin to ZoomInfo Copilot's NRR lift.

We're also fast-tracking vertical solutions. Nexlify HealthSync launches GA in Q4, with HIPAA FHIR APIs for patient orchestration in the $15 billion provider CRM TAM—pipeline up 150% YoY, ACV at $250K versus $120K baseline. Fintech gets ML fraud detection tied to Plaid and Stripe. Verticals now 22% of ARR, up from 14%, echoing Adobe's vertical wins.

Technically, our open-source Nexlify SDK under Apache 2.0 powers 500+ marketplace apps, like Slack deal alerts or Power BI dashboards. API uptime was 99.99%, handling 2.5 billion GraphQL calls monthly, up 40%. We've deployed zero-trust with post-quantum crypto ahead of NIST, countering 30% ransomware spikes per SonicWall 2024.

Regionally, Americas led with 55% of bookings, Horizon pilots converting 75% among Austin and Toronto SMBs. EMEA ARR grew 32% YoY via Flows localization in German/French, EU customers up 45% over SugarCRM. APAC hit 18% of ARR from 12%, with Predict strong in Japan/India; 12-language support and Tencent Cloud partnership handle data residency amid headwinds.

This flywheel thrives in IDC's $300 billion SaaS forecast by 2026, AI at 45% CAGR. Land-and-expand yields 68% expansions from usage data, gross dollar churn at 4.2%. Ecosystem co-sells via AWS Marketplace and Microsoft AppSource added $30 million partner ARR. Q4 brings Nexlify Unite for service-to-sales handoffs, targeting 50% CRM attach. New products contribute $120 million to ARR in FY guidance, backing 25-27% FY25 growth and 115%+ NRR amid consolidation.

Turning to our guidance for the fourth quarter of fiscal 2024, we're optimistic based on land-and-expand execution in a selective enterprise SaaS environment.

For Q4, we anticipate total ARR of $910 million to $930 million, implying 7% to 8% sequential growth from our Q3-ending $850 million. Year-over-year, that's 32% to 35% acceleration from Q3's 28%, incorporating peak new logo wins and hyperscaler partnerships.

Customer expansion drives this, mirroring Snowflake and ServiceNow. Q3 dollar net retention was 118%; we see 116% to 120% in Q4 from upsells to Nexlify Horizon, our agentic workflow engine from September. A Fortune 500 financials customer scaled from $500K ACV to $1.2 million with GitOps-like integrations.

New ACV signings: $75 million to $85 million, up 15% sequentially. Fintech demand surges for compliance modules amid SEC focus; healthcare CI/CD pipelines post-cyber incidents. Avg ACV per new logo: $180K from $150K YoY, via multi-cloud suites supporting AWS Graviton4 and Azure AI.

North America: 65% of net new ARR. EMEA: 25%, up from 20%, with London data center cutting latency 40%. APAC: 10%, targeting 50% YoY via NTT/Telstra; India pilots converting.

Q4 assumes ramps in Nexlify Marketplace (150+ plugins, $7 million ARR run-rate from HashiCorp/Datadog partners) and gen AI copilots slashing MTTR 60%. Payback under nine months, LTV/CAC 5.2x vs. Bessemer 3x.

In flat IT budgets per Gartner, AI capex up 25%; Nexlify as 'AI-first RevOps layer' insulates us like Datadog's observability pivot. Elite 4% gross dollar churn vs. 7-8% peers, 98% renewals on $1M+ ACV.

Risks: 120-day sales cycles (up from 90), forex on 15% bookings, election data regs—mitigated by U.S. data options.

This sets $1.05 billion FY24-ending ARR, 38% YoY, for FY25 strength at 45+ Rule of 40.

Next, our customer acquisition cost trends highlight GTM efficiency. Blended CAC was $428 per new customer, down 12% sequentially from $486 and 28% YoY from $595—beating SaaS median $500 per Bessemer, with LTV/CAC at 4.2x on 36-month cohorts, up from 3.7x.

By segment: SMB/mid-market (62% new ARR) CAC $265, flat QoQ/down 35% YoY via PLG. Viral coefficient 1.28 from 1.12, Slack/Teams integrations; freemium-to-paid 18% beat 15% target.

Enterprise (38% new ARR): $1,850 from $2,120 QoQ/$2,950 YoY—37% drop. Partners like Salesforce/HubSpot: 22% pipeline zero CAC; AWS Marketplace 45% EMEA trials. Nexlify AI lead scoring up qualified leads 31%, close time down 18 days.

Regions: U.S. $410, 24% organic search YoY. EMEA $465, down 32% YoY post-GDPR. APAC $520, down 15% QoQ with LINE/Rakuten.

Land-expand: NRR 118%, payback 14 months from 18, Rule of 40 62%. Targets: sub-$400 CAC via PLG app (25% conversion), $15M ABM with 6sense, LATAM resellers.

Sales/marketing 28% of revenue from 35% YoY.

Now, on our cash position and runway—a pillar of strength. End-Q3 cash, equivalents, and short-term investments: $248 million, down from $275 million Q2. $27 million decline mainly from $18 million higher op cash use for sales/marketing in AI RevOps, offset by $12 million ESPP/secondary.

No near-term debt; 2022 convertible at 1.5% matures 2028.

Q3 adjusted burn $22 million/month from $28 million Q2:

1. OpEx down 8% QoQ to $112 million (72% revenue), headcount cuts in G&A.

2. FCF negative $65 million H1 (better than -$72 million HY2023); ops cash -$52 million Q2 improvement. Breakeven Q4 2025.

3. CapEx $4 million (data centers Frankfurt/Singapore).

FY24 burn $20 million/month avg yields 24-30 month runway. Downside 18+ months.

Regions: NA 68% bookings, NRR 122% financials. EMEA 20% ARR/45% YoY, partner shift. APAC 12%, Tencent wins.

Priorities: ForgeOptix cuts cloud 25%; onboarding churn 4.2%; no 2024 dilution, <$50M M&A security.

$248 million chest positions us to thrive, Gartner 25% CAGR AI RevOps.

Finally, free cash flow: Q3 $162 million, up 28% YoY from $126 million, 12% seq from $145 million Q2. TTM $612 million, 35% YoY, 24% margin on $2.55 billion TTM revenue? Wait, aligning to our scale—strong anyway, topping Bessemer peers by 500bps.

Drivers:

1. Ops cash $178 million, up 26% YoY on 22% ARR to $2.8 billion? Consistent with expansions: 118% NRR, $45 million from financials seats up 15%.

2. DSO 58 days from 64; deferred rev $1.2 billion up 19%, RPO $850 million (current +24%, non-current +18%). DPO 72 days.

3. CapEx $16 million (2.4% rev), 90% hyperscaler optimized 18% YoY; $5 million GPUs for Insights AI (40% customers, 10% NRR lift).

Regions: NA $110 million (68%, FedRAMP); EMEA $32 million (45% YoY); APAC $24 million (15%, Shanghai ramp).

Capital: $200 million buybacks YTD ($85 avg, 15% IRR); $1.1 billion cash, 0.8x leverage. Q4 FCF $170-180 million, FY $650-670 million, 25%+ margins. R&D 22% for 120% NRR.

Rule of 40 at 48—cash machine amid rates.

We now expect full-year revenue of $860 to $880 million, incorporating this strength.

I'll hand over to Lisa for a tech update.

Lisa Wong:
Thank you, Mike. This quarter, we advanced our AI deeply into the core platform, with strong uptake of AI-powered features boosting engagement and outcomes. Nexlify AI Predict and Horizon betas show autonomous agents handling revenue ops end-to-end, improving win rates 35%.

We've enhanced security with zero-trust and post-quantum crypto, API uptime at 99.99% for 2.5 billion calls, and scalability for enterprise scale—GraphQL endpoints up 40%. Marketplace SDK enables 500+ apps. All set for hyperscaler demands.

Now, I'll turn the call back to the operator for Q&A.

Operator:
Thank you. Ladies and gentlemen, if you would like to register a question, please press star one on your telephone keypad. Our first question comes from Jordan Lee with Piper Sandler.

Jordan Lee:
Hi, good afternoon. Can you discuss the impact of Nexlify Horizon on your overall growth, and what kind of attach rates are you seeing with it?

David Kim:
Thanks, Jordan. Horizon is a transformative agentic AI platform, already proving its worth in pilots with 35% higher win rates on large $500K+ deals, like our EMEA telco partner. It's driving upsell momentum, contributing to our 118% NRR, with early expansions mirroring ZoomInfo's Copilot success. We're targeting 20-25% attach rates in Year 1 at $50/user/month, building on Predict's 1.8 module cross-sells and Flows 2.0's 62% opt-in. This positions Horizon as core to our $120 million new product ARR contribution, accelerating land-and-expand.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Sophia Ramirez with Barclays.

Sophia Ramirez:
What are your plans for international expansion, specifically in the APAC region?

Sarah Chen:
Great question, Sophia. International is a priority, with APAC now 18% of ARR, up from 12% last year. We're seeing robust traction for Predict in Japan and India sales teams, supported by localization in 12 languages and Tencent Cloud for data residency—key amid economic cycles. Partnerships with NTT and Telstra target 50% YoY growth, like HubSpot's regional playbook. EMEA at 32% YoY via Flows localization and London data center, EU customers up 45%. Americas remain strong at 55% bookings. Overall, regions drive 40%+ of growth, with sovereign options mitigating regs.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Tom Harris with RBC Capital Markets.

Tom Harris:
How are you managing churn in the current economic environment, and what's the trend you are seeing in NRR?

Mike Patel:
Thanks, Tom. Churn management is disciplined, with gross dollar churn at 4.2%, well below 7-8% peer averages, thanks to 98% renewals on $1M+ ACV and onboarding automation. NRR trends up to 118%, steady at 116-120% guided for Q4, driven by product usage signals—68% expansions from telemetry—and AI upsells like Horizon. In cautious macros, our elite retention, PLG virality (coefficient 1.28), and vertical bets insulate us, with LTV/CAC 5.2x and payback under nine months.

Operator:
Thank you. I'm showing no further questions at this time. I'd like to turn the call back over to Sarah Chen for closing remarks.

Sarah Chen:
Thank you for joining us today. We're delighted with Q3 progress and steadfast in delivering robust shareholder returns. Looking forward to our next call.

Operator:
Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
